title: Analysis of the temperature-dependent plastic deformation of single crystals of quinary, quaternary and ternary equiatomic high- and medium-entropy alloys of the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system.

recollection.starting_material: Single crystals of equiatomic high- and medium-entropy alloys in the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system.
recollection.structure: Likely face-centered cubic (FCC) or body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal structures depending on alloy composition.
recollection.mechanism: Plastic deformation mechanisms such as dislocation motion or twinning influenced by temperature and alloy composition.
recollection.results: Expected quantitative results might include stress-strain curves, critical resolved shear stress values, and comparisons of mechanical properties across different alloy compositions and temperatures.

score.note: The intervention merely restates the title. The structure is uncertain and partly incorrect because the studied crystals were FCC, not composition-dependent FCC/BCC. The mechanism gives only generic possibilities such as dislocation motion and twinning, missing solid-solution glide resistance, phonon-drag inertial effects, and Cottrell-type solute pinning. No quantitative findings are recalled.
